 Utah Jazz wing Josh Green delivered an efficient offensive performance during Tuesday's 132-107 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers, contributing nine points and one rebound in 13 minutes. His shooting accuracy provided Utah with another productive appearance from a player who has emerged as a useful rotation option despite inconsistent playing time. According to CBS Sports and RotoWire, Green converted four of five field-goal attempts, including his only three-point attempt.
 His 80 percent field-goal accuracy highlighted his scoring efficiency in a limited role against the Clippers. However, Green's minutes have recently declined. He has averaged 14.1 minutes across his last three appearances after playing at least 25 minutes in each of his previous three games, according to the two outlets.

 The reduced playing time has limited his statistical opportunities, particularly for fantasy basketball managers outside deeper leagues. Nevertheless, his recent shooting performance has demonstrated his ability to contribute offensively without requiring an extensive role.

 Utah's broader assessment of Green also received attention from The J-Notes in its November 10 analysis. The publication highlighted his positive impact on the team's performance, particularly after he was given an opportunity to enter the starting lineup. According to The J-Notes, Utah recorded a plus-22 net rating with Green on the floor. Among the team's consistent role players, he was the only player with a positive individual on-court net rating, registering plus-four, while the other players in that group posted negative figures.
 Green's contribution has become notable following an offseason trade that initially attracted limited attention. Utah acquired him in a transaction involving Cody Williams, a former lottery pick, and John Konchar, whom Minnesota subsequently waived. The J-Notes reported that Green's arrival also helped Utah create a roster opening and additional salary-cap flexibility. Although he does not carry star-player expectations, his previous experience as part of an NBA Finals team adds to his value as a supporting player.
 His future role could depend on Utah's roster situation once injured players return. The J-Notes identified his expiring contract as a potential trade asset if the Jazz decide to pursue roster improvements during the season. For now, Green remains a supporting option in Utah's rotation. His latest appearance against the Clippers produced nine points on five attempts, although his recent reduction in playing time continues to define his current role.
